_about: Flow Wolf: Vigilant — the class, its features, Body in the Current, the nine Tenets. Mechanics carried over from the SW5E Sentinel (3/4 Flow caster, d8); every line of text is Bad Eden's own. The twelve Vigils live in vigilant-vigils-*.json. Built by tools/build-packs.mjs.

classes.name: Flow Wolf: Vigilant

classes.description:
A man in a black coat steps into a doorway's shadow and isn't there anymore. He's at the far end of the hall when his quarry walks past, and he puts the hilt of an arc-blade against the back of the man's skull and thumbs it on and off. He's gone before the body finishes falling.

A woman runs the length of a burning street with a double-ended blade turning in front of her, and the rounds that were meant for her go into the dirt. She gets her bleeding student up by the collar and keeps running.

Somebody's cornered at the edge of the quarry with nowhere to go, and the Vigilant keeps coming: a cut, a step, a cut, a step. The last step is a shove, with nothing in it but current, and then there's nobody at the edge at all.

Vigilants are the Flow Wolves who go alone. They mix the current and the blade so finely that nobody can tell where one stops, and they turn up where they were not expected, which is usually behind you.

Between the Two

Where a Theurge studies the Flow and a Warden wears it, a Vigilant threads it: a little in the step, a little in the swing, a little in the way they're suddenly not where you were looking. They do the lodge's quiet work. A lot of it never gets a name.

Working Alone

Vigilants are famously hard to put on a team. Most are happiest with no backup and no one to explain themselves to, and where others cover their weak spots with friends, a Vigilant covers them with the current. They'll take orders, within reason, as long as nobody tells them how.

Making a Vigilant

When you make a Vigilant, decide what the Flow is to you and what you do when nobody's watching. Did a lodge train you, or did the current find you alone on a bad road? Are you an operative who found out there was something extra in you, or the something extra that learned to operate? How do you treat people weaker than you, and who would you let see you be kind?

Quick Build

Make Dexterity your highest ability score, then Wisdom or Charisma. Pick the Criminal or Outlander background.

Class Features

As a Vigilant, you gain the following class features.

Hit Points

Hit Dice: 1d8 per Vigilant level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 8 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per Vigilant level after 1st

Proficiencies

Armor: Light armor
Weapons: Simple weapons, martial weapons
Tools: One set of artisan's tools or one kit of your choice
Saving Throws: Dexterity, Charisma
Skills: Choose three from Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Arcana, Insight, Intimidation, Perception, Persuasion, Stealth, and Survival

Equipment

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) two martial weapons or (b) a martial weapon and a shield
  • (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) any simple weapon
  • (a) a burglar's pack or (b) an explorer's pack
  • Leather armor, an arc-blade hilt, and a dark coat that doesn't rustle

The Vigils

At 3rd level you choose a Vigil, the lodge's word for the work a Vigilant keeps. Your Vigil grants you features at 3rd, 7th, 13th, and 18th level.

features.name: Flowcasting
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Vigilant, 1st level

You learned the Flow the way you learned to move: by needing to. The powers you know are the ones that fit between a step and a swing.

Powers Known

You know three powers of your choice at 1st level, and you learn more as you gain levels, as shown in the Powers Known column of the Vigilant table. You can't learn a power whose level is higher than your Max Power Level. Whenever you gain a Vigilant level, you can also swap one power you know for another you qualify for.

Flow Points

You have a pool of Flow points equal to three times your Vigilant level, plus your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice). You spend them to cast powers (a power costs its level plus one; at-will powers are free) and to fuel Body in the Current. You regain all spent Flow points when you finish a long rest.

Max Power Level

Most powers can be cast above their own level for a bigger effect, at one extra Flow point per level, up to your Max Power Level as shown on the Vigilant table. Powers of 5th level and higher are heavy water for a Vigilant: you can cast each of them once, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

Casting Ability

Which ability you cast with depends on which way the power runs. Sephirotic powers use Wisdom. Qliphothic powers use Charisma. Unaligned powers use whichever of the two you prefer. Use that modifier whenever a power refers to your casting ability, when you set a saving throw DC for a power, and when you make an attack roll with one.

Power save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your casting ability modifier
Power attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your casting ability modifier

features.name: Nudged
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Vigilant, 1st level

The current leans on your choices a little, and it's usually right. You can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.

features.name: Body in the Current
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Vigilant, 2nd level

You can run the current through your whole body for the length of a breath. You learn three tricks: Slip, Second Edge, and Quick Feet. Each costs 1 Flow point and uses your Kinetic die, a d4 that grows as you gain Vigilant levels (d6 at 5th, d8 at 9th, d10 at 13th, d12 at 17th). You can use each trick only once per round.

Slip

When you're the target of an attack, you can roll a Kinetic die and add it to your AC against that attack (no action required). You can do this before or after the attack roll, but before the GM says whether it hits.

Second Edge

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can roll a Kinetic die and deal extra damage of the weapon's type equal to the roll.

Quick Feet

When you move on your turn, you can roll a Kinetic die and increase your speed by 5 feet times the roll until the end of your turn.

features.name: Tenets
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Vigilant, 2nd level

A Vigilant holds to a few things, and the current holds to them back. You adopt two Tenets of your choice from the list at the end of the class description, and you adopt more as you gain levels, as shown in the Tenets Known column of the Vigilant table.

Each Tenet gives you something that's always on, and something you can call up for a moment: a manifest. You can manifest your Tenets a combined total of twice, and more at higher levels as shown in the Tenet Manifests column. Spend a use of this feature each time you manifest one. You regain all spent uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Vigilant, 5th level

You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Always Moving
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Vigilant, 10th level

There's no gap between the current and the blade anymore. When you take the Dodge or Disengage action, or use your action to cast a Flow power, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

features.name: Slip the Noose
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Vigilant, 15th level

Things meant for you keep finding you already gone. When an effect forces you to make a saving throw, you can spend 2 Flow points to add your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one) to the save. If you do, you take no damage from the effect if you succeed, and only half damage if you fail.

features.name: Dead Center
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Vigilant, 20th level

You stand in the exact middle of the current and nothing moves you off it. Your Dexterity score increases by 2, and so does your Wisdom or Charisma score (your choice, made when you reach 20th level). Your maximum for those two scores increases by 2.

Also, once per turn, when you would roll a Kinetic die, you can take the maximum instead.

features.name: Dead Center: Dexterity and Wisdom
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Vigilant, 20th level

Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores each increase by 2, and your maximum for those scores increases by 2.

features.name: Dead Center: Dexterity and Charisma
features.description:
Flow Wolf: Vigilant, 20th level

Your Dexterity and Charisma scores each increase by 2, and your maximum for those scores increases by 2.

features.name: Tenet of the Agile
features.description:
Tenet

Walls and water are just more floor. You have a swimming speed and a climbing speed equal to your walking speed. When you make a long jump you can cover a number of feet up to twice your Wisdom or Charisma score (your choice), and when you make a high jump you can leap a number of feet up equal to 3 + twice your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice).

Manifest. As a bonus action, spend a Tenet manifest: for the next minute, opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage.

features.name: Tenet of the Artisan
features.description:
Tenet

Whatever your hands are good at, the current is good at too. Choose one of your skill or tool proficiencies. When you make an ability check with it, you can add half your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one).

Manifest. As an action, spend a Tenet manifest: for the next 10 minutes the bonus rises to your full Wisdom or Charisma modifier, and you can extend this Tenet to a second skill or tool.

features.name: Tenet of the Contender
features.description:
Tenet

You never needed the blade. Your unarmed strike damage goes up one step (1 to a d4, d4 to a d6, or d6 to a d8), and your unarmed strikes have the finesse property.

Manifest. As a bonus action, spend a Tenet manifest: for the next minute your unarmed strikes count as enhanced for getting past resistance and immunity to unenhanced attacks, and you can use your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice) in place of Strength on checks to grapple or escape a grapple.

features.name: Tenet of the Fighter
features.description:
Tenet

You fight one particular way and you fight it well. Choose a Fighting Style (the GM adds it to your sheet).

Manifest. As a bonus action, spend a Tenet manifest: for the next minute you fight with the full weight of that style behind you — you have advantage on the first attack roll you make each turn with a weapon that style covers.

features.name: Tenet of the Hunter
features.description:
Tenet

Dark is where you work. You have darkvision out to 60 feet; if you already had darkvision, its range increases by 30 feet.

Manifest. As a bonus action, spend a Tenet manifest: for the next minute you see normally in magical darkness, and you have blindsight out to 10 feet.

features.name: Tenet of the Steadfast
features.description:
Tenet

You don't swing at them. You put the blade where they're going to be. When you would make a melee weapon attack roll, you can instead make the target roll a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your attack bonus with the weapon). If you'd have advantage on the attack, the target has disadvantage on the save, and if you'd have disadvantage, it has advantage. On a failed save the target takes the weapon's normal damage and suffers anything else a hit would have done.

Manifest. As a bonus action, spend a Tenet manifest: for the next minute, a creature that succeeds on the save still takes half the weapon damage, and one that rolls a 1 takes the damage as if you'd rolled the maximum.

features.name: Tenet of the Titan
features.description:
Tenet

You can carry more than they think. You gain proficiency with medium armor.

Manifest. As a bonus action, spend a Tenet manifest: for the next minute you have advantage on ability checks and attack rolls that would move another creature by force, and the distance you move it increases by 5 feet.

features.name: Tenet of the Tranquil
features.description:
Tenet

Still water holds more than you'd think. When you finish a short or long rest, you gain temporary Flow points equal to half your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one). Temporary Flow points are spent first, and whatever's left is lost at the end of your next short or long rest.

Manifest. As an action, spend a Tenet manifest: you regain Flow points equal to half your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one).

features.name: Tenet of the Vigorous
features.description:
Tenet

What keeps you going isn't entirely meat. When you roll a Hit Die to regain hit points, you can use your Wisdom or Charisma modifier in place of your Constitution modifier.

Manifest. As an action, spend a Tenet manifest: you gain temporary hit points equal to half your Vigilant level + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one).
